nodes.text: Unresponsive patient from enclosed space + normal PaO2: measure carboxyhemoglobin via co-oximetry
Immediately apply 100% normobaric oxygen via tight non-rebreather mask
Indications for hyperbaric oxygen: loss of consciousness, carboxyhemoglobin > 25%, ischemic ECG changes, pregnancy
**Severe metabolic lactic acidosis or cardiac ischemia:** transfer immediately to hyperbaric chamber
**Mild symptoms without loss of consciousness or pregnancy:** continue normobaric oxygen until asymptomatic
Obtain serial ECG and troponin to screen for myocardial injury
Follow-up neuropsychological evaluation for delayed neurological sequelae (Parkinsonism, memory loss)

algorithm.title: End-of-life decision making in locked-in syndrome

nodes.text: Locked-in syndrome from pontine stroke: patient retains full consciousness and cognitive capacity
Establish reliable communication code (eye blinks or vertical gaze) to assess decision-making capacity
Patient demonstrates capacity: autonomous refusal of life support (ventilator and hydration) must be honored
**Family member objects or threatens litigation:** counsel family that competent patient autonomy legally supersedes surrogate wishes
Transition goal of care to comprehensive palliative comfort measures and symptom control
Administer intravenous opioids (morphine) and benzodiazepines to relieve air hunger and distress
Perform compassionate terminal extubation in peaceful setting with family present

nodes.text: Acute severe thigh pain + proximal quadriceps weakness + loss of patellar reflex: femoral neuropathy
Recognize diabetic etiology (diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy or isolated femoral mononeuropathy)
Perform electromyography and nerve conduction studies: active denervation in femoral-innervated muscles
Perform retroperitoneal and pelvic imaging (CT or MRI) to exclude compressive hematoma or mass
**Compressive retroperitoneal hematoma:** surgical or interventional evacuation
**Diabetic amyotrophy (microvascular ischemia):** optimize glycemic control + consider short-course immunotherapy
Physical therapy with knee bracing to prevent falls + neuropathic pain pharmacotherapy

nodes.text: Infantile developmental regression + irritability + spasticity + optic atrophy: suspect Krabbe leukodystrophy
Perform brain MRI: extensive bilateral white matter demyelination and degeneration
Confirm diagnosis: measure galactocerebrosidase enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Identify pathognomonic multinucleated globoid cells on histology or genetic GALC testing
**Pre-symptomatic or newborn screening diagnosis:** early hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
**Symptomatic infantile onset:** comprehensive multidisciplinary supportive and palliative care
Manage spasticity and seizures with baclofen and antiseizure medications

nodes.text: HIV/AIDS patient with distal burning paresthesias and allodynia: diagnose HIV sensory polyneuropathy
Screen for contributing causes: neurotoxic antiretrovirals (didanosine, stavudine), B12 deficiency, diabetes
Initiate first-line systemic neuropathic pharmacotherapy: oral nortriptyline or gabapentin
**Intolerant or unresponsive to tricyclics:** switch to pregabalin or duloxetine
**Severe refractory burning pain:** add low-dose topical capsaicin or short-term tramadol
Optimize antiretroviral therapy (suppressive ART without neurotoxic reverse transcriptase inhibitors)
Foot care education and routine neurological surveillance to prevent trophic ulcers

c-neuro-05-q050.hinge: Bilateral sensorineural deafness with vestibular ataxia following prolonged parenteral gentamicin defines aminoglycoside vestibulotoxicity and ototoxicity.

nodes.text: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss + oscillopsia + ataxia after gentamicin: aminoglycoside toxicity
Recognize mechanism: aminoglycosides accumulate in endolymph, destroying cochlear and vestibular hair cells
Perform formal audiometry: high-frequency bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Vestibular testing (caloric testing, video head impulse test): bilateral vestibular hypofunction
Discontinue aminoglycoside immediately if still active; damage is largely irreversible
**Severe disabling bilateral hearing impairment:** evaluate for bilateral cochlear implantation
Vestibular rehabilitation physical therapy to train visual and proprioceptive compensatory balance mechanisms
